title: Working parents share how they use AI to streamline tasks
excerpt: Working parents say AI platforms like ChatGPT and Claude help them manage schedules, freeing them up to spend more time with their kids.

8 working parents share how they use AI to give them more time with their kids

By Julia Pugachevsky

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

AI is already a divisive topic when it comes to the future of work. The discourse heats up even more the closer you get to home.

Last week week, Open AI CEO Sam Altman was torched for suggesting that parents could use ChatGPT to "have it make a podcast that talks about one kid's soccer game that afternoon, one kid's upcoming birthday, some news" on a drive to school. Hundreds of X users fanned the flames with the same question: Why not just talk to your kids?

While some parents worry about becoming overly reliant on AI, some see it as a powerful tool for managing packed schedules and overwhelming to-do lists. Some also find it helpful for troubleshooting their most specific parenting problems, whether they're concerned about a missed milestone or want to improve their kids' grades.

We asked eight parents how they use AI to balance work and family life, finding the technology frees them up to be more present for their children.

Hope Denton 'brain dumps' into ChatGPT to balance family and work responsibilities

Hope Denton is a 35-year-old mom of three kids, ages 6, 13, and 15, in Indiana. She's also juggling a remote content writing job, her photography company, freelance writing, contract projects, and volunteer work.

She told Business Insider that she balances all her tasks by brain-dumping into ChatGPT every night. "Instead of falling asleep, I'm mentally bouncing between work deadlines, appointments, practices, dinner, laundry, emails, and all the little things I am afraid I will forget by morning," she said.

ChatGPT then helps her find the most efficient ways to tackle everything, while also noting what can be put off for now.

Denton has also used ChatGPT to plan a week-long road trip through Arizona, including finding the best driving routes to avoid backtracking through the state.

"For me, it is less about having ChatGPT do the work and more about giving my brain room to breathe," Denton said. "It helps me stop staring at the finish line long enough to take the first step."

Hally Peck uses Perplexity and Claude to manage her family calendar and sign her kids up for camp

Hally Peck, a chief marketing officer at Addition Wealth in New York who is in her 30s, previously told Business Insider that while some AI prompts take time to set up, "automating some of these life tasks has given me more time on the weekends with my kids and has been a true win for me."

She took 10 minutes to vibe-code an AI agent via Perplexity to order groceries every Sunday based on the brands her family likes, flagging anything out of stock. She also uses a Perplexity agent to automatically fill our forms and sign her kids up for activities like camp.

She also programmed Claude to streamline everyone's schedules into one family Google calendar and note potential conflicts.

She hopes to create more AI agents in the future. "It would be amazing to say everything is running 100% on AI, but you still need to put the work in to get it to the output you want," she said.

Christopher Domanski created a ChatGPT voice tutor for his daughters

Christopher Domanski is a 41-year-old working dad of two daughters, ages 6 and 8. Domanski, who works as a director of business management & development at a manufacturing facility in California, said it can be time-consuming to balance work with all other aspects of parenting.

"That's where I've kind of embraced AI to save time," Domanski told Business Insider.

When Domanski noticed that his daughters' progress reports had some gaps, he created custom, voice-activated ChatGPT tutors to continually quiz them in spelling and math until they understood the subject material.

Domanski also uses ChatGPT to digitize paper handouts from the school. Every week, he takes photos of flyers and permission slips and has ChatGPT extract the dates and action items before putting them into a Microsoft Outlook calendar.

"For me, the value is not that AI replaces parenting or teaching," Domanski said. "It reduces the administrative and repetitive work so I can focus more attention on the parts that actually require a parent."

Sara Sprong designs physical activity books and game boards using ChatGPT

Like many parents, Sara Sprong, 40, uses AI to help with organizing her family schedule, meal-planning, and fine-tuning vacation itineraries.

But her favorite use of the platform is for hands-on projects for her three kids, ages 4, 8, and 9.

Sprong, who works in customer success at a UX research technology company in Colorado, said she always has broad ideas for family activities. "The challenge isn't a lack of creativity," she told Business Insider. "It's finding the time and mental bandwidth to bring those ideas to life."

On a big family trip up north to Wisconsin, she came up with custom Mad Libs tied to activities they were doing and a scavenger hunt around the resort. She asked ChatGPT to format everything into 8" x 11" sheets of paper so she could print them into physical books.

To reduce her children's screen time, she also makes game boards of different household activities they can complete before they can use their iPads or watch TV.

"It really helps me narrow down all the endless choices and be more intentional with my time," Sprong said.

Cara Katz uses Claude to plan her week and order groceries

Cara Katz, a 36-year-old working mom, has been using AI for almost six years, including for help with parenting tasks.

"Since I've started using it at home, I've saved myself at least 10 hours a week," Katz previously told Business Insider. "I'm tired of being judged for it."

Katz, who works from home and takes her daughter to enrichment activities like music and library events, says she uses Claude to make a color-coded Google calendar to keep her family's schedules organized. Additionally, Katz uses Claude to keep an inventory of her pantry and has it connected to DoorDash and UberEats to order groceries.

She also loves using Claude to predict when her daughter should hit different milestones, with suggested activities to help reach her goals.

Katz said AI gives her more time with her daughter. " We are buying back time with our kids using AI," she said. "My mental workload has lightened."

Ijeoma Nwaogu meal-preps and assigns chores using ChatGPT

Prior to using AI, Ijeoma Nwaogu felt overwhelmed with balancing work with parenting her three kids.

"I was struggling to find some sense of harmony in managing my time, my energy level, my work schedule, and my kids' needs," Nwaogu previously told Business Insider.

Nwaogu uses ChatGPT to design custom daily schedules for her kids, including finding family-bonding activities to do together in-between stretches of time. She also loves using it to create recipes based on what she has in the kitchen and what each family member likes.

ChatGPT also comes up with age-appropriate chores for each of her kids, including options attuned to what her kids already like to do (such as decluttering or organizing things by color).

Nwaogu said ChatGPT helped her get rid of her "mom guilt." "I can now spend more time with my kids," she said. "I'm less stressed and feel like a better mom."

Janine Clements loves her ChatGPT 'coach'

Janine Clements, a full-time working mom of two teen daughters, uses ChatGPT to tackle more nuanced issues in the home, such as reconnecting with her 14-year-old daughter when she was spending a lot of time in her room or introducing a phone-free zone.

She also likes using it for recipe ideas that adhere to everyone's preferences and find teen-bonding activities like volunteering at an animal shelter together.

"It's way more intuitive than Google because you can refine your prompts as you go along," Clements previously told Business Insider. For example, she said ChatGPT gave her family more unique spots to visit in London.

"Although I know ChatGPT, or any other AI platform, shouldn't replace a parent's own judgment, it's lightened my load, helped me handle parenting headaches, and made everyday life just that little bit easier," Clements said.

Katrina Beebe uses Claude to track her daughter's milestones

Katrina Beebe, a 29-year-old mom who works in supply chain logistics in Illinois, uses Claude to balance her full-time work responsibilities with raising her 18-month-old daughter.

When she first returned to work after her maternity leave, Beebe had her parents and a few family members watch her daughter before transitioning her to daycare. To make things easier for everyone, Beebe initially tracked her daughter's schedule and had Claude create a custom schedule based on the average times her daughter napped or fed.

"As a parent, you have limited time," Beebe told Business Insider. "You don't really think about what you're doing in the moment necessarily and those patterns over time."

She also programmed an AI agent, trained on specific information about her daughter, to track her progress in different milestones. If she's not hitting them, Beebe asks for advice on how she can help, whether it's by expanding her daughter's vocabulary or dealing with picky eating. She said she uses AI about 2 to 3 times a day, including for other household questions around interior design and landscaping.

Beebe said AI helps her continue to perform at the levels she wants when she's spread thin. "Because I have probably the least amount of time that I've ever had in my 29 years, I still want to get the same amount of workload done in my work life and in my personal life," she said.

8 位在职父母分享他们如何利用人工智能让自己有更多时间陪伴孩子

作者：Julia Pugachevsky 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

当谈到未来的工作时，人工智能已经是一个存在分歧的话题。 离家越近，讨论就越激烈。

上周，Open AI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 因建议家长在开车去学校的路上可以使用 ChatGPT“让它制作一个播客，谈论一个孩子当天下午的足球比赛、一个孩子即将到来的生日以及一些新闻”而受到批评。 数百名 X 用户都提出了同样的问题：为什么不直接和你的孩子谈谈呢？

虽然一些家长担心过度依赖人工智能，但也有一些家长认为它是管理日程安排和繁重待办事项列表的强大工具。 有些人还发现它有助于解决他们最具体的育儿问题，无论他们是担心错过里程碑还是想要提高孩子的成绩。

我们询问了八位家长如何使用人工智能来平衡工作和家庭生活，发现这项技术可以让他们腾出更多时间陪伴孩子。

希望 Denton 将“大脑倾倒”到 ChatGPT 以平衡家庭和工作责任

霍普·丹顿 (Hope Denton) 是印第安纳州的一位 35 岁母亲，三个孩子的年龄分别为 6 岁、13 岁和 15 岁。 她还兼顾远程内容写作工作、摄影公司、自由写作、合同项目和志愿者工作。

她告诉《商业内幕》，她每天晚上都通过 ChatGPT 来平衡所有的任务。 “我的精神不是入睡，而是在工作截止日期、约会、训练、晚餐、洗衣、电子邮件以及所有我担心早上会忘记的小事情之间来回跳动，”她说。

然后，ChatGPT 帮助她找到解决所有问题的最有效方法，同时还指出现在可以推迟的事情。

Denton 还使用 ChatGPT 计划了穿越亚利桑那州的为期一周的公路旅行，包括寻找最佳驾驶路线，以避免在该州走回头路。

“对我来说，重要的不是让 ChatGPT 完成工作，而是给我的大脑提供呼吸的空间，”丹顿说。 “它帮助我不再盯着终点线太久，从而迈出第一步。”

Hally Peck 使用 Perplexity 和 Claude 来管理她的家庭日历并为她的孩子报名参加夏令营

30 多岁的纽约 Addition Wealth 首席营销官 Hally Peck 此前告诉《商业内幕》，虽然一些人工智能提示需要时间来设置，但“自动化其中一些生活任务让我在周末有更多时间陪伴孩子，这对我来说是真正的胜利。”

她花了 10 分钟通过 Perplexity 对人工智能代理进行振动编码，以便每周日根据家人喜欢的品牌订购杂货，并标记所有缺货的商品。 她还使用 Perplexity 代理自动填写我们的表格，并为她的孩子报名参加露营等活动。

她还对克劳德进行了编程，将每个人的日程安排简化到一个家庭谷歌日历中，并记录潜在的冲突。

她希望未来创造更多的人工智能代理。 她说：“如果说一切都 100% 依靠人工智能运行，那真是太神奇了，但你仍然需要付出努力才能达到你想要的输出。”

Christopher Domanski 为他的女儿们创建了 ChatGPT 语音导师

克里斯托弗·多曼斯基 (Christopher Domanski) 是一位 41 岁的职业父亲，有两个女儿，分别为 6 岁和 8 岁。 多曼斯基在加利福尼亚州一家制造工厂担任业务管理和开发总监，他表示，平衡工作与养育子女的所有其他方面可能非常耗时。

“这就是我采用人工智能来节省时间的地方，”多曼斯基告诉《商业内幕》。

当多曼斯基注意到女儿们的进度报告存在一些差距时，他创建了定制的声控 ChatGPT 导师，不断地对她们进行拼写和数学测验，直到她们理解了主题材料。

Domanski 还使用 ChatGPT 将学校的纸质讲义数字化。 每周，他都会拍摄传单和许可单的照片，并让 ChatGPT 提取日期和行动项目，然后将它们放入 Microsoft Outlook 日历中。

“对我来说，价值不在于人工智能取代了育儿或教学，”多曼斯基说。 “它减少了行政和重复性工作，因此我可以将更多注意力集中在实际需要父母的部分。”

Sara Sprong 使用 ChatGPT 设计体育活动书籍和游戏板

和许多父母一样，40 岁的萨拉·斯普朗 (Sara Sprong) 使用人工智能来帮助安排家庭日程、膳食计划和微调假期行程。

但她最喜欢使用该平台的是为她的三个孩子（年龄分别为 4、8 和 9 岁）进行实践项目。

Sprong 在科罗拉多州一家用户体验研究技术公司从事客户成功工作，她说她对家庭活动总是有广泛的想法。 “挑战并不在于缺乏创造力，”她告诉《商业内幕》。 “它正在寻找时间和精神带宽来将这些想法变为现实。”

在一次前往威斯康星州北部的大型家庭旅行中，她想出了与他们正在进行的活动以及在度假村周围进行寻宝游戏相关的定制疯狂自由。 她要求 ChatGPT 将所有内容格式化为 8 英寸 x 11 英寸的纸张，以便她可以将它们打印成实体书。

为了减少孩子们看屏幕的时间，她还制作了不同家庭活动的游戏板，让他们可以在使用 iPad 或看电视之前完成这些活动。

“这确实帮助我缩小了所有无尽的选择范围，并且更加有意识地利用我的时间，”斯普朗说。

卡拉·卡茨 (Cara Katz) 使用克劳德 (Claude) 来计划她的一周并订购杂货

卡拉·卡茨 (Cara Katz) 是一位 36 岁的职业妈妈，她已经使用人工智能近六年了，包括帮助完成育儿任务。

“自从我开始在家使用它以来，我每周至少节省了 10 个小时，”Katz 此前告诉 Business Insider。 “我厌倦了因此而受到评判。”

卡茨在家工作，带女儿参加音乐和图书馆活动等丰富活动，她说她使用克劳德制作了一个用颜色编码的谷歌日历，以让家人的日程安排井井有条。 此外，Katz 使用 Claude 来保存她的食品储藏室的库存，并将其连接到 DoorDash 和 UberEats 来订购杂货。

她还喜欢使用克劳德来预测她的女儿何时应该达到不同的里程碑，并提供建议的活动来帮助她实现目标。

卡茨说人工智能让她有更多时间陪伴女儿。 “我们正在利用人工智能来买回与孩子们在一起的时间，”她说。 “我的精神负担减轻了。”

Ijeoma Nwaogu 使用 ChatGPT 准备饭菜并分配家务

在使用人工智能之前，Ijeoma Nwaogu 因平衡工作与抚养三个孩子而感到不知所措。

恩瓦奥古此前对《商业内幕》表示：“在管理我的时间、我的精力水平、我的工作安排和我孩子的需求方面，我一直在努力寻找某种和谐的感觉。”

Nwaogu 使用 ChatGPT 为她的孩子们设计定制的日常安排，包括在空闲时间一起寻找增进家庭联系的活动。 她还喜欢用它根据厨房里的东西和每个家庭成员的喜好来创建食谱。

ChatGPT 还为她的每个孩子提供了适合年龄的家务，包括适合孩子已经喜欢做的事情的选项（例如整理或按颜色组织东西）。

Nwaogu 说 ChatGPT 帮助她摆脱了“妈妈的负罪感”。 “我现在可以花更多时间陪伴我的孩子，”她说。 “我的压力减轻了，感觉自己是一个更好的妈妈。”

Janine Clements 喜欢她的 ChatGPT “教练”

Janine Clements 是一位有两个十几岁女儿的全职妈妈，她使用 ChatGPT 来解决家庭中更微妙的问题，例如当她 14 岁的女儿在房间里待了很长时间时与她重新联系，或者引入无电话区。

她还喜欢用它来制作符合每个人喜好的食谱创意，并寻找青少年联系活动，例如一起在动物收容所做志愿者。

克莱门茨此前告诉《商业内幕》：“它比谷歌更直观，因为你可以在操作过程中完善提示。” 例如，她说 ChatGPT 为她的家人提供了更多伦敦独特的景点。

“虽然我知道 ChatGPT 或任何其他人工智能平台不应该取代父母自己的判断，但它减轻了我的负担，帮助我解决了育儿难题，并使日常生活变得更加轻松，”克莱门茨说。

卡特里娜·毕比 (Katrina Beebe) 使用克劳德 (Claude) 来追踪女儿的里程碑

Katrina Beebe 是一位 29 岁的妈妈，在伊利诺伊州从事供应链物流工作，她利用 Claude 来平衡她的全职工作职责和抚养 18 个月大的女儿。

当毕比产假结束后第一次重返工作岗位时，她让她的父母和一些家庭成员照顾她的女儿，然后将她转移到日托中心。 为了让每个人都更轻松，Beebe 最初跟踪了她女儿的日程安排，并让 Claude 根据她女儿午睡或吃饭的平均时间创建了一个自定义日程安排。

“作为父母，你的时间有限，”毕比告诉《商业内幕》。 “你并没有真正思考你此刻正在做什么以及随着时间的推移这些模式。”

她还编写了一个人工智能代理程序，根据有关她女儿的特定信息进行训练，以跟踪她在不同里程碑上的进展。 如果她没有打他们，毕比会询问如何提供帮助，无论是扩大女儿的词汇量还是解决挑食问题。 她说她每天大约使用人工智能 2 到 3 次，包括解决有关室内设计和景观美化的其他家庭问题。

Beebe 说，当她的身体分散时，人工智能可以帮助她继续保持她想要的水平。 “因为我的时间可能是 29 年来最少的，所以我仍然希望在工作生活和个人生活中完成同样多的工作量，”她说。
